question: What is the main goal of post-abortion care (PAC) counselling?

options.A: To punish clients who break hospital rules
options.B: To force clients to speak with law enforcement
options.C: To support clients physically and emotionally
options.D: To convince clients to change their religious beliefs

explanation: PAC counselling is all about giving compassionate physical and emotional support to help your client heal safely. As a nurse, creating a safe space makes all the difference! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h1)

question: Why is a non-judgmental approach so important when caring for a post-abortion client?

options.A: Clients often face stigma, fear, and guilt
options.B: It lowers the cost of medical supplies
options.C: It is required by the hospital billing department
options.D: It shortens the length of hospital stays

explanation: Many clients carry heavy emotional burdens like fear and societal stigma. A welcoming, open-hearted nurse helps build the trust they need to heal. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h1)

question: What does 'values clarification' help a nurse examine?
explanation: Values clarification is a great self-check tool. It allows us as nurses to look at our own inner biases so our personal opinions never get in the way of great patient care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h2)

question: How should you handle your personal moral beliefs when caring for a post-abortion client?

options.A: Refuse to provide any medication or comfort
options.B: Put personal views aside to deliver respectful care
options.C: Report the client to religious leaders
options.D: Argue with the client about their life choices

explanation: Professional nursing ethics mean we always put our patient's health and dignity first, delivering unbiased, compassionate care no matter our personal background. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h2)

question: What is a key physical sign you must check for during an initial post-abortion assessment?
explanation: Checking for heavy or excessive bleeding is a vital first step to catch potential hemorrhage early and keep your patient safe. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h3)

question: A client is quiet, avoids eye contact, and trembles slightly during your assessment. What might this suggest?

options.A: The client is ready for immediate hospital discharge
options.B: The client is hiding a contagious respiratory infection
options.C: The client may be experiencing significant emotional distress
options.D: The client has a normal blood pressure reading

explanation: Withdrawn behavior and physical trembling are classic signs of anxiety, fear, or emotional shock. A gentle touch and supportive counselling go a long way here! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h3)

question: Which symptom is a major danger sign that requires immediate medical help after an abortion?

options.A: Feeling slightly tired in the afternoon
options.B: Light spotting that stops after three days
options.C: Mild cramping for twenty minutes in the morning
options.D: Soaking through two heavy pads per hour for two hours

explanation: Heavy bleeding soaking multiple pads in a short time is a red flag for hemorrhage. Always act fast and notify the doctor on duty! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h4)

question: A client asks when it is safe to have sexual intercourse again after an abortion. What is the best advice?

options.A: Wait exactly one full year before trying again
options.C: Resume immediately if there is no headache
options.D: Wait until bleeding stops completely and the cervix closes

explanation: Advise 'pelvic rest' until bleeding stops and the cervix closes. This simple rule prevents bacteria from entering and drastically cuts down the risk of infection. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h4)

question: How soon can a person's fertility return after an abortion procedure?

options.B: Not for at least two years

explanation: Surprise! Ovulation can bounce back in as little as two weeks. That's why talking about family planning early is so crucial before she leaves the clinic. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h5)

question: Why is client-centered contraceptive counselling so important during post-abortion care?

options.A: It forces the client to use surgical sterilization
options.B: It helps the client freely choose a method that fits her life
options.C: It reduces the amount of paperwork for the clinic
options.D: It guarantees that the client will never need healthcare again

explanation: Client-centered care respects autonomy. We help her pick a method that matches her personal lifestyle and goals without pressure or judgment. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h5)

question: What are some common emotional reactions a client might experience after an abortion?
explanation: Emotions are complex and vary widely. A client might feel relief, sorrow, or a mixture of many things—and all of these responses can be completely normal. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h6)

question: When should you refer a post-abortion client to a mental health specialist?

options.A: When the client shows signs of severe depression or suicidal thoughts
options.B: Whenever the client has a mild headache
options.C: Every single time a client asks for a prescription for pain medicine
options.D: Only when the client refuses to take iron tablets

explanation: While basic emotional support is part of everyday nursing, deep psychological distress, severe depression, or self-harm threats need expert psychiatric help. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of community referral pathways in post-abortion care?

options.A: To keep clients inside the hospital for months
options.B: To connect clients with extended support and specialized services
options.C: To force clients to change their home addresses
options.D: To increase the cost of local pharmacy drugs

explanation: Referrals link clients to outside resources like support groups and community counsellors so they continue to get holistic care even after leaving the ward. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a goal of a strong healthcare referral network?

options.A: Isolating the client from all family and friends
options.C: Providing access to professional social workers
options.D: Connecting the client with community support groups

explanation: Good referral networks are designed to build a strong safety net and reduce isolation, never to cut a client off from the people who love and support them. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h7)
